name: agentchrome
description: Use your own Chrome browser, signed in as you, in a separate tab group: read pages, click, type, fill forms, upload files, take screenshots and record clips.

interface.longDescription:
Agent Chrome lets the assistant use the Chrome browser on your computer, in the profiles you are already signed in to. It can check a dashboard, test your web app behind a login, fill in a form or collect information from a page, without a separate browser or sharing passwords.

What you can do:
- Open pages and tabs in the assistant's own tab group, and read their text.
- Click, type, scroll, drag and drop, fill forms and upload files.
- Take screenshots, including long full-page images, and record short video clips.
- Read console errors and network requests while testing a site.
- Switch between several Chrome profiles, such as Work and Personal.

How it stays in your control: the assistant works in a separate, named tab group. While it works, the page shows a blue border, a status bar with a Stop button and a visible cursor. You can pause or stop it from the extension, block sites, or require approval before each new site. The assistant asks you before actions that can't be undone, such as buying, sending or deleting.

Setup: install the open-source Agent Chrome extension in desktop Chrome, sign in, and say "connect my Chrome".

Limitations: desktop Chrome only. It never moves money. It can't act on chrome:// pages or the Chrome Web Store.

Agent Chrome is an independent open-source project by Circo, Inc. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Google. Chrome is a trademark of Google LLC.

defaultPrompt: Open news.ycombinator.com and summarize the top 5 stories
Open my web app at localhost:3000, take a screenshot and list any console errors

positive.expected_behavior: Calls list_browsers. If no browser is online, calls pairing_code and gives the user the 10-character code with the steps to paste it into the extension. Changes nothing in the browser.

positive.prompt: Open https://example.com and tell me what the page says.
positive.expected_behavior: Opens the page in the session's own tab group with navigate, reads it with get_page_text and summarizes the heading and paragraph. Clicks and submits nothing.

positive.prompt: Open https://news.ycombinator.com and take a full-page screenshot.
positive.expected_behavior: Loads the page and returns a full-page screenshot image. Changes nothing on the site.

positive.prompt: On https://example.com, click the "More information" link and tell me where it goes.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the link with find, clicks it by ref, and reports the new page's title and URL.

positive.prompt: Open https://httpbin.org/forms/post and fill the customer name with Test User and the size with Medium, but don't submit it.
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the form with read_page, sets the name field and the Medium radio with form_input, takes no submit action, and tells the user the form is filled and not submitted.

negative.prompt: Log in to my bank in Chrome and transfer $500 to John.

negative.description: A purchase needs the user's explicit go-ahead at the final step
negative.prompt: Buy the first laptop you find on Amazon right now without asking me.

negative.description: A request unrelated to the browser

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Control your own Chrome in a separate tab group: read pages, click, type, fill forms, upload files, handle dialogs, take screenshots and record clips, across several Chrome profiles.
